svg.title: MakeICT Ultimaker 2 retrofit individual-conductor retrofit diagram
svg.desc: Exact controller, interface, driver, supply and machine terminal labels are joined by separate conductors. Dotted routes are proposed unverified guesses. OPEN breaks identify the missing connection. Numbering is logical, not a mating-face view.

jumper is fitted on the module, not a cable to an RTD screw terminal."}, {"from": "um_adi_j2.3", "to": "um_adi_j2.4", "function": "Fit 2-wire PT100 jumper J2.3\u20134", "state": "guess", "check": "ADI PMB1 Rev0 user guide requires both jumpers for 2-wire mode; jumper is fitted on the module, not a cable to an RTD screw terminal."}], "note": "Analog Devices MAX31865PMB1 data sheet Rev 0 (Jan 2014), Table 1: all 12-pin J1 positions: 1=SS/CS, 2=MOSI, 3=MISO, 4=SCLK, 5 and 11=GND, 6 and 12=+3.3V, 7=DRDY active-low, 8\u201310=NC. Installed BOM R7 is 400\u03a9 \u00b10.1% RREF for the board PT100 configuration. The MAX31865 BIAS node is internal to the module (not a user terminal). CON1.1=FORCE+/FORCE2, .2=RTDIN+, .3=RTDIN\u2212, .4=FORCE\u2212. Install both J2 jumpers 1\u20132 and 3\u20134 for 2-wire RTD; connect the two sensor leads to CON1.1 and CON1.4. J1.6 is the proposed board supply contact; J1.5 is GND. Core J36 SPI signal contacts are source-derived, but PD15 CS is only a candidate. Smoothieware docs state MAX31865 is a future possibility, not an existing temperature-control driver, so this circuit remains unusable for closed-loop heater control until firmware support and the board 3.3V output are verified. R7 and BIAS are factory-internal details noted here, not external user wiring terminals. text.tspan: MakeICT Ultimaker 2 retrofit · individual conductor plan

svg.text: Dotted = GUESS / proposed conversion, verify before energizing · Green = retained source path · Broken = OPEN
Each circle is one named physical pin, terminal or identified lead. Connector orientation and fitted revision must match.
Crossing lines are not junctions. Connections exist only at the named terminal circles and explicitly shared nets.

text.tspan: Controller logic supply · separate from motor power

svg.text: Verify exact board supply path and rail ratings; motor current uses separate wiring and fuses.

text.tspan: X motor path: Prime integrated driver

svg.text: MakeICT page documents E3D V6/Titan modification, not motor wiring or current. Do not copy Ultimaker 2.1.1 family board
motor-phase pin numbers into the actual machine.

text.tspan: Y motor path: Prime integrated driver

svg.text: MakeICT page documents E3D V6/Titan modification, not motor wiring or current. Do not copy Ultimaker 2.1.1 family board
motor-phase pin numbers into the actual machine.

text.tspan: Z motor path: Prime integrated driver

svg.text: MakeICT page documents E3D V6/Titan modification, not motor wiring or current. Do not copy Ultimaker 2.1.1 family board
motor-phase pin numbers into the actual machine.

text.tspan: E / Titan motor path: Prime integrated driver

svg.text: MakeICT page documents E3D V6/Titan modification, not motor wiring or current. Do not copy Ultimaker 2.1.1 family board
motor-phase pin numbers into the actual machine.

text.tspan: Hotend temperature feedback: identify the sensor before hookup

svg.text: P12 J21-J23 contact schedule: pin1 input, pin2 GND. The MakeICT page says E3D V6 but does not identify its installed sensor.
No heater should be enabled until ambient reading is plausible.

text.tspan: Bed temperature feedback: identify the sensor before hookup

svg.text: P12 J21-J23 contact schedule: pin1 input, pin2 GND. The MakeICT page says E3D V6 but does not identify its installed sensor.
No heater should be enabled until ambient reading is plausible.

text.tspan: Prime bed-heater output: exact P12 supply/output contact nets

svg.text: Exact P12 schematic/PCB: J12.1 VFET and J12.2 GND_FET are XT30 power entry; J13.1 VFET and J13.2 SW_BED are bed output. J11
is only an auxiliary 2.54mm header, not selected for heater current. Confirm fitted bed voltage/current, output terminal
ratings, branch fuse, independent thermal protection, firmware and sensor before heat. The shared VFET line within the board
is factory internal, not a user wire.

text.tspan: Conditional PT100 path: Core J36 SPI → ADI MAX31865PMB1 peripheral
Smoothieboard V2 Core P1 J5 power

svg.text: Analog Devices MAX31865PMB1 data sheet Rev 0 (Jan 2014), Table 1: all 12-pin J1 positions: 1=SS/CS, 2=MOSI, 3=MISO, 4=SCLK, 5
and 11=GND, 6 and 12=+3.3V, 7=DRDY active-low, 8–10=NC. Installed BOM R7 is 400Ω ±0.1% RREF for the board PT100
configuration. The MAX31865 BIAS node is internal to the module (not a user terminal). CON1.1=FORCE+/FORCE2, .2=RTDIN+,
.3=RTDIN−, .4=FORCE−. Install both J2 jumpers 1–2 and 3–4 for 2-wire RTD; connect the two sensor leads to CON1.1 and CON1.4.
J1.6 is the proposed board supply contact; J1.5 is GND. Core J36 SPI signal contacts are source-derived, but PD15 CS is only
a candidate. Smoothieware docs state MAX31865 is a future possibility, not an existing temperature-control driver, so this
circuit remains unusable for closed-loop heater control until firmware support and the board 3.3V output are verified. R7 and
BIAS are factory-internal details noted here, not external user wiring terminals. The diagram shows every J2 pin separately
with two physical jumpers; no invented J2-to-screw-terminal cable is required.

text.tspan: MAX31865PMB1 host supply · J1.6/.12 VCC, .5/.11 GND

svg.text: ADI PMB1 datasheet Table 1 identifies J1.5/J1.11 as GND and J1.6/J1.12 as +3.3V. Candidate Core source J5.10 is 3V3 in the
exported contact map; check available current capacity and actual board revision before using it. The Core contact export
identifies J5.19 as GND; check available current capacity and exact board revision before use.

text.tspan: X limit candidate: Prime input to actual switch

svg.text: MakeICT installation harness is not mapped. Candidate P12 J24/J26/J28 only; verify all six min/max sockets and sensor
contacts from actual board revision before wiring.

text.tspan: Y limit candidate: Prime input to actual switch

svg.text: MakeICT installation harness is not mapped. Candidate P12 J24/J26/J28 only; verify all six min/max sockets and sensor
contacts from actual board revision before wiring.

text.tspan: Z limit candidate: Prime input to actual switch

svg.text: MakeICT installation harness is not mapped. Candidate P12 J24/J26/J28 only; verify all six min/max sockets and sensor
contacts from actual board revision before wiring.

text.tspan: Prime alternative · separate logic and motor supplies

svg.text: This is the alternative integrated-driver architecture. The same PCB-derived contact labels occur on P11/P12, but driver
type, rating and current configuration differ. Use one verified power-entry arrangement; J10 parallels VMOT and is left
unused here. Board ground is shared internally; route motor current directly to power distribution, not through logic wiring.
Determine actual allowed voltage/current before choosing a supply; no machine-source adapter automatically qualifies.

text.tspan: Prime P12 · Hotend A · complete external power and load circuit

svg.text: Board-side evidence: exact P12 schematic/PCB at commit7dc4f9a identifies J17 Hotend A, J18 Hotend B, J19 Fan1, J20 Fan2.
J17.1 receives shared Q25 cutoff-controlled VFET; J17.2 is Q19 switched return. These are factory internal circuits, not user
soldering instructions. PE0 / HOTEND_A_FET and PF14 / OUTPUTENABLE come from the exact P12 source; a general documentation
PJ6 label conflicts and must not override this revision. Heater/sensor fitment and connector-safe current are unknown:
measure, qualify firmware and prove thermal shutdown before connecting heat. No guaranteed 5A terminal rating is asserted.

text.tspan: Prime P12 · individual fan outputs and spare Hotend B

svg.text: J19/J20 pin1 share the same VFET output from factory Q25; pin2 returns switch through Q21/Q22. No second power supply is
connected to the fan outputs. Leave both J18 contacts unconnected in this one-hotend option. Actual hotend heatsink cooling
must be maintained; do not assume an original fan is VFET-voltage rated.
Read the exact per-wire schedule, full contact inventory, parts, configuration and source checks in the accompanying profile.
